https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.teaser: When it comes to adding stripes to your wardrobe, where do you draw the line? Vertical? Horizontal? Both? How many colours are too many? And that’s before we’ve even started on width. Whether on shirts, tees, jackets or ties, stripes are a smart move this season – when colour and pattern can really carry an outfit – but perilously easy to get wrong. Here’s a guide to learning your lines.

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.title: Three Ways To Wear Utility Trousers
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.teaser: Utility trousers come in all shapes, forms and functions. Cargo styles were initially made for soldiers; carpenter and painter’s trousers were designed to fit tools while fatigue pants were cut to facilitate movement and durability. Despite their humble beginnings, the drawstring waists, patch pockets, tool loops and a field-inspired coloured palette of utility trousers have all left their mark on everyday dressing. Today, they are championed by anyone from heritage workwear labels to luxury brands and more contemporary designers. The result is an offering that’s as varied as its origins – and just as adaptable.

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.title: Everything You Need To Know About Dress Shoes
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.teaser: Avoid brown in town. Or after 6.00pm. And never do business with a man in loafers. These are some of the shoddy truisms our grandfathers taught us as callow lads. We also remember the intoxicating confusion of entering a proper bootmaker’s for the first time. The experience was not that different to being hungry and in need of a stiff drink in a foreign land. Staring at the array of bench-made shoes as a well-meaning salesman prattled on was as disconcerting as that Scandinavian misadventure when we thought we ordered a steak and received cold mackerel.

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.title: The Elevated Essentials Every Man Should Have This Autumn
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.teaser: A change of season calls for a change of clothing. And as temperatures drop, extra layers are required. Enter what we like to refer to as the essentials. The foundations that you put on then forget about. Which isn’t to say they don’t deserve your full attention. What constitutes an essential? These will be the building blocks of your wardrobe going into the new season – but they can also be out of the ordinary.

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.title: The Japanese Brands To Know Now
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.teaser: A trip to Japan can be a lesson in humility. You may think that what you’re wearing is considered. Well put together, even. Then, as you saunter through the streets of Tokyo, you encounter a workman. Just a random guy, fixing a rare pothole in the road. And you come to the realisation that his outfit is considerably more put together than yours.

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.title: A Guide To The Best Knitwear For Sweater Weather
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.teaser: Knitwear? Knit-everywhere, more like. With the arrival of what can be officially classified as “sweater weather”, it’s worth remembering that other options are available. And also that knitwear has changed. Or hasn’t. You see, a woollen jumper isn’t just an adaptable layer for unsettled conditions, it’s also a piece that is open to reinterpretation. And, boy, have some designers reinterpreted it.

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.title: Why TOTEME Deserves A Space In Your Wardrobe
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.teaser: Considering the immediate resonance and now-cult following of its women’s collection, 12 years is quite a substantial amount of time to wait before making a menswear line. But for TOTEME, it was also the point.The Stockholm label built its reputation on certain archetypes – the scarf jacket, the cocoon coat, structured tailoring – and on the conviction that a wardrobe earns its authority and trust slowly, piece by piece, rather than all at once. That same sense of discipline, says cofounder Karl Lindman, is exactly what made the brand hold off on menswear for so long – and now test it on new ground.

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/w.title: How NOMOS Glashütte Became The Watch Nerd’s Watch Brand
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/w.teaser: If you’re not massively into watches, there’s a decent chance that NOMOS Glashütte isn’t one of the first names that comes to mind. Rolex, sure. Omega, probably. Cartier, absolutely. But spend enough time around people who are really into watches and, sooner or later, someone will start telling you all about this small, independent German brand. “Once you become a watch enthusiast, you’ll hear other watch people whisper about NOMOS,” says watch collector Bill Adler. “And when you put one on, you’ll understand what those quiet accolades are about.”

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.title: Everything A Man Should Know About Keeping His Wardrobe In Great Shape
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.teaser: Sourcing the finest clothes known to humankind is one thing. Keeping them that way is another entirely. And where you’d expect to come to MR PORTER for the former, we have some thoughts on the latter, too. From a general guide to making your clothes last longer to more specific instructions that focus on sneakers, coats, watches and knitwear, below is an exhaustive compendium on wardrobe maintenance.

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/l.title: 15 Ways To Give Your Home A Facelift
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/l.teaser: A man’s home, famously, is his castle. Figuratively, at least. A place you retreat to every night, a respite from the outside world. So, there’s every reason to put the time, money and effort into creating a space that works for your needs – and in which you (and anyone who happens to pass through) can really enjoy luxuriating. We asked the experts for their top tips for elevating a space, whether it’s a sprawling countryside estate or a minimal one-bed apartment in the city. Think of your entrance space as a room in itself. “Add colour and texture – a dark entrance can be incredibly dramatic,” says the New York-based interior designer Robert Passal.

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.title: The Clothes That Made Johnny Marr
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.teaser: In the last month, Johnny Marr parted ways with the guitar heard in “This Charming Man” and many other songs by The Smiths. The 1982 Rickenbacker 330 Jetgo was among the star lots in an auction of more than 70 instruments hosted by Christie’s. And while it was key to Marr’s signature sound, he won’t be losing any sleep over selling it. Clothing, however, was notably absent from the sale. “I’d actually find it harder to get rid of some of my jackets than I would some of my guitars,” Marr tells MR PORTER. “Oh man, I’m getting a visceral reaction even thinking about it.”

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.title: The Style Debate: Celebrate The Return Of Skinny Jeans Or Stick To Looser Cuts?
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.teaser: From the arrival of The Strokes and Hedi Slimane in the early 2000s for a good decade or so, you couldn’t move for skinny jeans. (This was certainly true if you were sporting a particularly tight pair.) And then, almost overnight, they just vanished – into thin air, appropriately enough – while more capacious trousers moved in. However, if you thought you’d seen the back pocket of snug denim, think again. The cyclical nature of fashion, multiplied by the revolving door of trends in the age of algorithms means that no item of clothing is gone for long. And so, if rumours – and runways – are true, then skinny jeans are due a return. Should we just suck it up and embrace this comeback? Two correspondents have opposing thoughts. Here’s the skinny.

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.title: How To Play The Long (Sleeves) Game
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.teaser: Until not long ago, the long-sleeved T-shirt lived quietly beneath other things – occupying the category of layers that you put on for warmth and rarely thought about again. But the return of the early-2000s wardrobe has brought it back to the fore. Worn on its own, it now does the work of a considered outfit. And it does so with very little effort required from you.

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.title: Three Ways To Break Up A Suit
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.teaser: A suit is a fine thing, but a matching one can sometimes feel a tad too predictable. Enter spezzato, the Italian art of splitting a suit into separate pieces and wearing them apart. The word loosely translates as “broken”, though there is nothing damaged about the result. This logic is a natural fit for Neapolitan tailoring, where soft, unstructured jackets already hold their own. However, it works with sharper tailoring, too. The difference between doing it right and looking like you’ve lost half the suit comes down to three adjustments, below.

In January – a month of relentless rain, sub-zero mornings and a post-holiday financial hangover – we embark upon radical self-reinvention. It’s not only unrealistic (the sunlight deficiency!), it’s borderline masochistic.

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.teaser: There’s a very good chance that you aren’t reading this. Or, in fact, very much at all. “Numerous studies show that reading is in free-fall,” the journalist James Marriott wrote on Substack last year. “Even the most pessimistic 20th-century critics of the screen-age would have struggled to predict the scale of the present crisis. In America, reading for pleasure has fallen by 40 per cent in the last 20 years. In the UK, more than a third of adults say they have given up reading.”

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.title: The Softer Side Of Mr P.
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.teaser: New York has got a reputation. Fast paced and direct to the point of brusque. It is known for its hard edges. And against this colourful – in all senses of the word – setting, Mr P.’s new AW26 collection can’t help but stand out. “It has gotten softer this season,” says Emily Grieves, Design Manager at Mr P. “That was a key part of it – the dropped shoulders and softer fabrics.”

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.title: How To Wear Technical Gear With Smarter Looks
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.teaser: There was a time when wearing a technical shell jacket with tailored trousers suggested one of two things: you’d either been caught in unexpectedly bad weather on your way to the office or you were on your way somewhere to do something practical. But today, that is no longer the case. Performance clothing has spent the past decade muscling its way into everyday wardrobes. GORE-TEX jackets are quotidian, trail shoes double up as fashion shoes and climbing bags spend more time in coffee shops than they do up a mountain.

Seven Things To Look Out For During Frieze Week
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/l.teaser: Every October, London’s Regent’s Park becomes the centre of the art world – and the city around it follows. Between the fairs, the gallery openings, the talks and the parties, there’s a lot to take in. The temptation can be to head straight to the household names, or heavy-hitting solo artists. But the best of Frieze Week is not necessarily found in the most obvious places. It lies in the moments when an ordinary object becomes unfamiliar, a painting unsettles our assumptions, or a space changes the way we experience art that stays with you long after the week is over. These seven presentations below offer precisely that: an invitation to look again.

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.title: Behind The Scenes At MR PORTER’s AW26 Shoot In New York
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.teaser: The most cinematic city in the US arguably isn’t Los Angeles, even if that’s where the movie industry is supposedly centred (although increasingly isn’t). It’s New York. And if LA has made it its business to pretend to be somewhere else, New York is always inexcusably, iconically itself.

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.title: The Enduring Legacy Of Timberland
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.teaser: In 1973, Massachusetts bootmaker Nathan Swartz injection-moulded a waterproof leather boot for New England construction sites and forestry crews. Nobody involved in the making of that Timberland eight-inch boot (the classic six-inch would be released three years later) could have predicted that this piece of unglamorous utility would become one of the most quietly influential objects in street style. It was claimed, in turn, by Milanese paninari, Bronx MCs, Compton rappers and London ravers, each group shaping its meaning to fit their own cultural code.

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.title: Moncler Revisits Its Most Iconic Jackets with Re/Icons
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.teaser: Moncler’s best stories start high up in the mountains. On 31 July 1954, Italian alpinists Achille Compagnoni and Lino Lacedelli became the first people to reach the summit of K2, the world’s second-highest peak, as part of an Italian expedition led by geologist Ardito Desio. Moncler, then a young outerwear label founded in the French Alps just two years earlier, had outfitted the team with its Karakorum jacket.

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.title: How To Reset Your Wardrobe For Autumn
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.teaser: Former US President Barack Obama always wore the same outfits. Why? So he could spend time on more important things. Unlike us, he didn’t want to be lying awake at night worrying about whether his new Bengal-striped shirt went better with unwashed or faded denim. “You’ll see I wear only grey or blue suits,” Obama told Vanity Fair in 2012. “I’m trying to pare down decisions. I don’t want to make decisions about what I’m eating or wearing. Because I have too many other decisions to make.”

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.title: The New Rules Of Country Dressing
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.teaser: In recent years, country life has changed. And so, we’re updating our guidance on what to wear when venturing beyond the metropolis for the weekend. Back in the 2010s, dressing for the country was still governed by ideas that were more Downton than downtown, long after old-fashioned rural lifestyles had gone from feeling aspirational to looking anachronistic. What has happened since? A combination of the pandemic, the mania around England’s Cotswolds, full-fibre broadband, remote working and the cost of urban property has produced a demographic shift – and you can now lead a 21st-century life in the country.

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/l.title: 15 Ways To Be A Better Morning Person
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/l.teaser: Morning people wake from their sleep with ungrudging ease. They’re at their most productive when the sun has barely got out of the starting blocks. It’s because their brains are most alert and their body clocks perfectly primed for being creative and industrious. And there’s plenty of scientific evidence to show that having a positive wake-up routine comes with a whole load of physical and mental health benefits.

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.title: The Rise Of The Lived-In Wardrobe
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.teaser: What, this old thing? Of all the trends we’ve seen in menswear over the past couple of years, there has been one constant: aged and well-loved clothing. The likes of Austin Butler, Jeremy Allen White and Jacob Elordi are often spotted wearing pieces that look as though they’ve previously seen action on a dusty ranch. But what is it about vintage clothes that’s so appealing? Is it tapping into a lifestyle that isn’t our own? Or just that these clothes have seen some things before they reach us.

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.title: What To Pack For An Autumn Getaway
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.teaser: We’re at the midway point between the end of summer and the winter holidays. For those at school, it’s known as a half-term. However, the rest of us have earnt our own autumnal equivalent of a spring break. Fall break is our working title. (Not to be confused with a breakfall, which will get you out of mischief in judo.) Now, if there’s one thing we know about autumn, it’s that it can be a tricky season to pin down (those ne-waza holding techniques proving ineffective). Elsewhere, we have a list of 11 items for everything right now will throw at you.

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.title: The Ascent Of The Modern Hiking Boot
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.teaser: Start at the bottom and work your way up. No, we’re not giving out career advice or describing the property ladder – it’s Style 101. It doesn’t matter where you’re heading, paying extra attention to your footwear is crucial as it can have a real impact on how your day pans out. And one of the most important items on your shoe rack? Your hiking boots. Going out into the wild, or even just the park for a dog walk, requires footwear that protects. Keeping you warm and dry is the objective.

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.title: Is The Footwear Of The Moment Finally A Proper Shoe?
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.teaser: Something is afoot in the fashion world. “At the recent shows, I was really struck by how few sneakers there were,” reports Lauren Cochrane, senior fashion writer at The Guardian. “The footwear seemed to be focused on brogues, loafers and Derby shoes. Basically, nothing with an air bubble or a colour. And as big and chunky as possible.” “Sneakers will always have a place on the streets, but the variety of trending styles seems less prevalent than it once was,” agrees Rachel O-Williams, Assistant Personal Shopper at MR PORTER.

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.title: Be The Main Character With TOM FORD
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.teaser: TOM FORD has always known that a suit looks best with a bit of attitude. It’s an idea that runs through the label’s approach to tailoring, which is front and centre of its latest collection, exclusively at MR PORTER. The codes are familiar but the mood is looser than you might expect – shirts are open at the collar, silk scarves are wrapped around without too much thought and leather trousers sit under a double-breasted jacket, so everything stays polished without ever feeling stiff.

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.title: A Weekend In The Langhe With Canali
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.teaser: Come October, the southern area of Italy’s Piedmont region, Langhe, fills up with truffle hunters. Before dawn, they head into the oak and hazel woods around Alba with their dogs, looking for the white truffle that has made this corner of northern Italy famous. It’s muddy, patient work, and the mist is still sitting low in the valleys when it starts. We don’t mean to brag, but if you’ve got a couple of pieces from our exclusive Canali capsule to hand, you pretty much have all you need for hunting truffles yourself.
